category: Mixed-signal simulation analyses, sources, models & signal integrity analysis
description: The SPICE-based circuit simulator driven from the Simulation Dashboard (analysis types, sources, probes, models, measurement and SPICE options) and the PCB Signal Integrity analyser (screening, reflection, crosstalk, IBIS models, termination advisor).

tools.name: Operating Point Analysis
tools.description: DC bias-point solution with capacitors open and inductors shorted; results (node voltages, branch currents, device power) are displayed directly on the schematic and in the SimData document. Runs automatically before Transient unless Use Initial Conditions is enabled. Node Set (.NS) and Initial Condition (.IC) devices seed the solver.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Analysis Setup & Run > Operating Point > Run; display Voltage / Power / Current checkboxes
tools.example: Enable Operating Point, tick Voltage and Current, Run: every net shows its DC voltage next to the wire.
tools.notes: Convergence failures are usually cured by GMIN stepping options or adding a Node Set.

tools.name: DC Sweep Analysis
tools.description: Series of operating-point solutions while one or two source values (or global parameters) sweep From/To/Step, producing transfer curves such as Vout vs Vin or Ic vs Vce families. Up to two sweep parameters may be enabled; the secondary sweep produces a curve per step.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > DC Sweep > add parameter (source or global parameter) > From / To / Step > Run

parameters.name: Parameter
parameters.description: Source (e.g. V1) or global parameter to sweep.

tools.example: Sweep V1 from 0 to 5 V step 0.01 V and plot V(OUT) to obtain the comparator threshold.
tools.notes: Add a Voltage Probe on the output net beforehand; results open in the .sdf waveform document.

tools.name: Transient Analysis
tools.description: Time-domain simulation over an interval (From/To/Step) or a number of periods (N Periods / Points per Period), with Use Initial Conditions to skip the operating point and optional Fourier Analysis (fundamental frequency, number of harmonics) of the results. Output resembles an oscilloscope trace for each probed node.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Transient > Interval (From/To/Step) or Period mode > optional Fourier Analysis > Run

parameters.name: From / To / Step
parameters.description: Simulation window and maximum time step.

parameters.name: Use Initial Conditions
parameters.description: Start from .IC values instead of the DC operating point.

parameters.name: Fourier Analysis
parameters.description: Fundamental Frequency and Number of Harmonics for THD.

tools.example: Transient 0 to 10 ms, step 1 us, Fourier at 1 kHz with 10 harmonics to read THD of an audio amplifier.
tools.notes: Step size limits accuracy; use Advanced options TMAX or reduce Step for fast edges.

tools.name: Fourier Analysis (Transient option)
tools.description: Computes the amplitude and phase of harmonics of the transient waveform at a given fundamental frequency, reporting THD and the harmonic table in the SimData document. Enabled as a checkbox inside the Transient analysis.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Transient > Fourier Analysis checkbox > Fundamental Frequency / Number of Harmonics

parameters.name: Fundamental Frequency
parameters.description: Base frequency of the periodic signal.

tools.example: Fundamental 1 kHz, 20 harmonics, transient of at least several periods: the results tab lists THD %.
tools.notes: Simulate enough full periods after settling for accurate results.

tools.name: AC Sweep Analysis (frequency response)
tools.description: Small-signal frequency sweep from Start to End Frequency with Linear, Decade or Octave point distribution, computing magnitude/phase (Bode) of probed nodes after linearising the circuit at its operating point. Requires an AC Magnitude (and optional phase) on at least one source. Noise Analysis is an option of this analysis.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > AC Sweep > Start Frequency / End Frequency / Points, sweep type > Run

parameters.name: Sweep Type / Points
parameters.description: Linear | Decade | Octave and number of points.

tools.example: V1 with AC Magnitude 1, AC Sweep 10 Hz to 10 MHz, Decade, 100 points; plot Magnitude(dB) and Phase(Deg) of V(OUT).
tools.notes: Use output expressions such as db(v(out)) or Phase(Deg) functions in the SimData waveform editor.

tools.name: Noise Analysis (AC Sweep option)
tools.description: Computes input- and output-referred noise spectral density (V^2/Hz) across the AC sweep for a chosen Noise Source, Output Node and Reference Node, summarising contributions per device every Points Per Summary steps.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > AC Sweep > Noise Analysis checkbox > Noise Source / Output Node / Ref Node / Points Per Summary

parameters.name: Noise Source
parameters.description: Input source the noise is referred to.

tools.example: Noise Source V1, Output Node OUT, Ref 0, 10 points per summary: plot ONOISE and INOISE.
tools.notes: Device models need noise parameters (e.g. resistor thermal noise is automatic; op-amp macromodels may lack it).

tools.name: Transfer Function Analysis
tools.description: DC small-signal transfer function between a Source Name and a Reference Node: gain, input resistance and output resistance are reported as scalar results. Quick way to characterise DC gain and impedances of amplifiers and dividers.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Transfer Function > Source Name / Reference Node > Run
tools.example: Source V1, Reference Node OUT: results show Transfer Function 2.0, Input Resistance 10 k, Output Resistance 50 ohm.
tools.notes: Linear analysis only; nonlinear behaviour needs DC Sweep.

tools.name: Pole-Zero Analysis
tools.description: Finds the poles and/or zeros of the small-signal transfer function between input and output node pairs (V(out)/V(in) or V(out)/I(in)), reporting them in the results table for stability and compensation work.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Pole-Zero > Input Node / Input Reference / Output Node / Output Reference > Analysis Type (Poles Only | Zeros Only | Poles and Zeros) > Transfer Function Type > Run

parameters.name: Analysis Type
parameters.description: Poles Only | Zeros Only | Poles and Zeros.

tools.example: Input IN/0, Output OUT/0, Poles and Zeros, V(out)/V(in) for an active filter to verify pole placement.
tools.notes: Large circuits can be slow; reduce to the relevant sub-circuit.

tools.name: Temperature Sweep
tools.description: Repeats the enabled analyses (Operating Point, DC/AC Sweep, Transient, Transfer Function, Noise) for each temperature From/To/Step in degrees Celsius, applying device temperature coefficients (TC1/TC2, semiconductor models) to show drift.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Temperature Sweep > From / To / Step > Run with another analysis enabled
tools.example: Sweep -40 to 85 step 25 with Operating Point to see the reference voltage drift.
tools.notes: Default TEMP/TNOM is 27 degC in Advanced options.

tools.name: Parameter Sweep
tools.description: Steps a component value, model parameter or global parameter over a range (Linear, Decade, Octave or explicit List) and repeats the enabled analyses for each value, plotting a family of curves. Subcircuit-internal values cannot be swept directly (use a global parameter passed into the subcircuit).
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Parameter Sweep > Parameter (component/parameter) > Sweep Type / From / To / Step or List > Run

parameters.name: Parameter
parameters.description: e.g. R3 value or {Rload} global parameter.

tools.example: Sweep C2 from 1 nF to 100 nF Decade 3 points with AC Sweep to view filter corner movement.
tools.notes: Global parameters are placed with the Parameters simulation directive or a .PARAM text.

tools.name: Monte Carlo Analysis
tools.description: Runs the enabled analyses N times with component values randomly varied within tolerances (per-component Tolerance parameter or default tolerances for resistors, capacitors, inductors, transistors, DC sources, digital tp) using Uniform, Gaussian or Worst Case distributions and a random Seed, to estimate yield/spread of a measurement.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Monte Carlo > Number of Runs / Distribution / Seed / default tolerances > Run

parameters.name: Default tolerances
parameters.description: Resistor, Capacitor, Inductor, Transistor, DC Source, Digital Tp percentages.

tools.example: 100 runs, Gaussian, resistor tolerance 1%, capacitor 10%, AC Sweep: overlay of cutoff frequencies; add a measurement CutoffLow to tabulate.
tools.notes: Per-part tolerance overrides come from the component's Tolerance parameter.

tools.name: Sensitivity Analysis
tools.description: Calculates how much each component value influences selected output measurements (DC or AC), using group or custom deviations, ranking components by sensitivity so tolerances can be assigned where they matter.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Sensitivity > Group Deviations / Custom Deviations > select measurements > Run

parameters.name: Group Deviations
parameters.description: Percent change applied per component group.

parameters.name: Measurements
parameters.description: Output quantities whose sensitivities are computed.

tools.example: Sensitivity of the Max measurement of V(OUT) to all resistors with 1% deviation: R7 dominates, so specify it as 0.1%.
tools.notes: Availability depends on the release (Altium Designer 22+).

tools.name: S-Parameters Analysis (Open Beta)
tools.description: Frequency-domain N-port analysis using Port definitions (default 50 ohm) that yields S-, Y- and Z-parameters, plotted with expressions s_<m>_<n>, y_<m>_<n>, z_<m>_<n> (e.g. s_2_1 in dB). Offered as an open-beta feature in recent releases.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > S-Parameters > define ports (impedance) > frequency range > Run; plot s_2_1
tools.example: Two ports across a matching network, 100 MHz to 3 GHz; plot Magnitude(dB) of s_1_1 to view return loss.
tools.notes: Enable the feature in Advanced Settings if the analysis is not visible.

tools.name: Stress Analysis (component stress, Open Beta)
tools.description: Evaluates each component's operating conditions (voltage, current, power, temperature) from the simulation against stress model limits and derating coefficients defined per component, flagging overstressed parts in a results table.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Stress Analysis > configure stress models/derating > Run with Transient or Operating Point
tools.example: Run Transient with Stress Analysis: R4 shows 120% of rated power during start-up and is flagged.
tools.notes: Requires stress parameters on the components (from templates or manual entry).

tools.name: VSRC / ISRC (DC voltage and current sources)
tools.description: Basic DC sources from the Simulation Generic Components library: VSRC (voltage) and ISRC (current) with Value, plus AC Magnitude and AC Phase parameters for AC Sweep. Used for supplies and bias; DC Sweep can sweep their value.
tools.usage: Components panel > Simulation Generic Components > VSRC / ISRC; parameters Value, AC Magnitude, AC Phase
tools.example: VSRC 'VCC' Value 5; VSRC 'VIN' Value 0 with AC Magnitude 1 for a Bode plot.
tools.notes: Ground the circuit with the GND power port named '0' (or the SIM GND) - the simulator requires node 0.

tools.name: VPULSE / IPULSE (pulse sources)
tools.description: Periodic pulse sources with DC Magnitude, AC Magnitude/Phase, Initial Value, Pulsed Value, Time Delay, Rise Time, Fall Time, Pulse Width and Period parameters - the standard clock/step stimulus for transient analysis.
tools.usage: Simulation Generic Components > VPULSE / IPULSE

parameters.name: Time Delay / Rise Time / Fall Time / Pulse Width / Period

tools.example: VPULSE 0 V to 3.3 V, delay 0, rise/fall 2 ns, width 50 ns, period 100 ns for a 10 MHz clock.
tools.notes: Rise/fall must be non-zero for convergence; a single step is a pulse with a very long width.

tools.name: VSIN / ISIN (sinusoidal sources)
tools.description: Sine sources with Offset, Amplitude, Frequency, Delay, Damping Factor and Phase, plus AC Magnitude/Phase for AC sweeps; used for audio/RF transient stimulus and distortion (Fourier) tests.
tools.usage: Simulation Generic Components > VSIN / ISIN
tools.example: VSIN amplitude 10 mV, frequency 1 kHz into a preamp; Transient 5 ms with Fourier at 1 kHz.
tools.notes: Set AC Magnitude 1 on the same source to reuse it for AC Sweep.

tools.name: VPWL / IPWL (piece-wise linear sources)
tools.description: Arbitrary waveform defined by time/value pairs (typed in the Time/Value Pairs parameter or loaded from a file) with optional repeat; used for ramps, brown-out profiles and captured waveforms.
tools.usage: Simulation Generic Components > VPWL / IPWL; parameter Time/Value Pairs = (0 0) (1m 0) (1.1m 5) (5m 5)

parameters.name: File / Repeat
parameters.description: External PWL file and repetition options.

tools.example: VPWL (0 0) (2m 0) (3m 12) (10m 12) to model a 12 V supply ramp and check inrush current.
tools.notes: Times must be increasing; use engineering suffixes (m, u, n).

tools.name: VEXP / VSFFM (exponential and single-frequency FM sources)
tools.description: VEXP/IEXP produce an exponential rise then decay (Initial/Pulsed Value, Rise Delay/Time Constant, Fall Delay/Time Constant) for RC-like stimuli; VSFFM/ISFFM produce a single-frequency frequency-modulated carrier (Offset, Amplitude, Carrier Frequency, Modulation Index, Signal Frequency) for demodulator tests.
tools.usage: Simulation Generic Components > VEXP / IEXP / VSFFM / ISFFM

parameters.name: VEXP: Rise/Fall Delay and Time Constant
VSFFM: Carrier Frequency / Modulation Index / Signal Frequency

tools.example: VSFFM carrier 100 kHz, index 5, signal 1 kHz feeding a PLL demodulator; Transient 5 ms.
tools.notes: Other generic sources include VAM/IAM (amplitude modulated), VRAND (random), BVSRC/BISRC (behavioural, expression-based) and controlled sources E/F/G/H.

tools.name: Behavioural and controlled sources (BVSRC/BISRC, E/F/G/H, switches)
tools.description: Expression-driven and dependent sources: BVSRC/BISRC evaluate a SPICE expression such as V(IN)*2 or IF(V(A)>1,5,0); E (VCVS), F (CCCS), G (VCCS), H (CCVS) linear dependent sources with gain; voltage- and current-controlled switches (SW/CSW) with threshold/hysteresis models; and equation-defined nonlinear sources for behavioural modelling of blocks without SPICE models.
tools.usage: Simulation Generic Components > BVSRC, BISRC, the dependent sources (SPICE E/F/G/H devices: VCVS, CCCS, VCCS, CCVS) and the switch models (SW, CSW)

parameters.name: Expression (BVSRC/BISRC)
parameters.description: Behavioural formula using node voltages/currents and functions.

parameters.name: Gain (E/F/G/H)
parameters.description: Linear gain of the dependent source.

tools.example: BVSRC with expression 'V(IN)*V(IN)' realises a squaring block for a power-detector simulation.
tools.notes: Expressions support the same function set as the waveform editor (ABS, EXP, LIMIT, PWL, TABLE, IF).

tools.name: Simulation model types (SPICE .mdl / .ckt, SimModel, digital SimCode)
tools.description: A component simulates through its SIM model link: a .mdl (SPICE .MODEL card, e.g. diode/BJT/MOSFET parameters), a .ckt (SPICE .SUBCKT, op-amps, regulators, complex parts), built-in generic device kinds (resistor, capacitor, sources), or SimCode digital models (.scb/.txt) for logic devices. The Sim Model dialog (component > Models > Sim) sets Model Kind, Model Sub-Kind, Spice Prefix, pin mapping (Port Map) and parameters; Netlist Template shows the emitted line.
tools.usage: Component Properties > Models > Add > Simulation; Model Kind (Transistor, Diode, Op-Amp, Passive, Sources, Digital...) > Model File / Parameters / Port Map

parameters.name: Model File (.mdl/.ckt)
parameters.description: SPICE model text; must be findable via project/search paths or the same folder.

parameters.name: Port Map
parameters.description: Schematic pin to SPICE node order mapping.

tools.example: Link LM358.ckt to an op-amp symbol, map pins IN+, IN-, V+, V-, OUT in the subcircuit's node order, check Netlist Preview shows XU1 ... LM358.
tools.notes: Simulation Dashboard's Preparation region lists parts with missing/invalid models; vendor PSpice/LTspice models often need syntax cleanup (see PSpice import).

tools.name: PSpice / LTspice model import (Import SPICE models)
tools.description: Vendor .lib/.cir files written for PSpice or LTspice can be linked as .ckt/.mdl models; the simulator accepts most PSpice syntax (Simulation Dashboard offers a PSpice compatibility mode) but unsupported constructs (some digital primitives, .PROBE, vendor-specific functions) must be edited. Workflow: copy the model into the project folder, add a Sim model link pointing to it, map ports, then verify in the dashboard's model check.
tools.usage: Component > Models > Add Simulation > Model File = vendor.lib (subckt name) ; Simulation Dashboard > Preparation > Verify models

parameters.name: Subcircuit name
parameters.description: Name of the .SUBCKT to use from the file.

parameters.name: PSpice compatibility
parameters.description: Dashboard/advanced option to accept PSpice-specific syntax.

tools.example: Download the TPS7A02 PSpice model, save as TPS7A02.ckt in the project, link it, run Operating Point to confirm output voltage.
tools.notes: Encrypted vendor models cannot be used; behavioural models with many nodes slow transient runs.

tools.name: Sim probes: Voltage, Current, Power, Differential Voltage
tools.description: Probe directives placed on the schematic from the Simulation toolbar or the Simulation Dashboard's Add buttons that define which waveforms are collected and plotted: Voltage probe on a net (V(net)), Current probe on a pin, Power probe on a component, and Differential Voltage probe between two nets; probes are listed in the Simulation Dashboard's Preparation region and can be enabled/disabled per analysis.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Preparation > Add probes (Voltage / Current / Power / Differential Voltage), or the Simulation toolbar probe buttons; click on a wire/pin
tools.example: Place a Voltage probe on OUT and a Current probe on R1 pin 1, run Transient: both traces appear in the .sdf document.
tools.notes: Without probes the simulator collects all nodes (Collect Data For All Signals) which can be slow on big circuits.

tools.name: Advanced Analysis Settings (SPICE options)
tools.description: Dialog from the Simulation Dashboard's Settings button with SPICE simulator options: tolerances ABSTOL, VNTOL, RELTOL (1e-3), CHGTOL, PIVTOL/PIVREL, GMIN, iteration limits ITL1-ITL5 (100, 50, 4, 40, 5000), TEMP/TNOM (27 degC), integration method (Trapezoidal or Gear with order), TMAX, default device parameters, and options such as Spice Reference Net Name, digital supply/threshold settings and convergence aids (GMIN stepping, source stepping).
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > Settings (Advanced Analysis Settings)
tools.example: Convergence failure in a switching regulator: set RELTOL 0.01, ITL4 100, Method Gear order 2, re-run Transient.
tools.notes: Loosening tolerances trades accuracy for convergence; document changes in the simulation profile.

tools.name: Waveform expressions and measurements (SimData functions)
tools.description: The SimData (.sdf) editor evaluates expressions over waveforms: algebraic (+ - * / MOD ABS), logarithmic (DB, LOG10, EXP, SQRT, POW), trigonometric, integral (AVG, RMS, DDT, IDT), complex for AC (Magnitude, Magnitude(dB), Real, Imaginary, Phase(Deg/Rad), Group Delay) and misc (LIMIT, TABLE, PWL, MAX, MIN). Measurements (Add Measurement) compute scalars such as BandWidth, CutoffLow/High, CenterFrequency, QualityFactor, RiseTime, FallTime, Period, Frequency, Max, Min, Peak, Valley, XatMax, YatX, DeltaY, RangeY, AVG, Rms, Slope, Width.
tools.usage: SimData document > Add Wave to Plot > expression, e.g. db(v(out)/v(in)) ; Add Measurement > RiseTime(v(out))

parameters.name: Expression
parameters.description: Waveform algebra using v(net), i(device), functions.

parameters.name: Measurement
parameters.description: Named scalar computed over the trace, tabulated per run in sweeps.

tools.example: Plot 'Magnitude(dB)(v(out))' and add measurement CutoffLow to read the -3 dB point; in Monte Carlo the measurement histogram is shown.
tools.notes: Number formats accept engineering suffixes (f p n u m k meg g t) and scientific notation.

tools.name: Node Set (.NS) and Initial Condition (.IC) directives
tools.description: Simulation directives from the Simulation Generic Components library: Node Set suggests a starting voltage for a net to help the operating-point solver converge (then released), while Initial Condition forces the node voltage at t=0 for transient runs when Use Initial Conditions is enabled (e.g. pre-charged capacitors, oscillator kick-start).
tools.usage: Place .NS / .IC component on the net, set Voltage parameter; Transient > Use Initial Conditions for .IC

parameters.name: Voltage
parameters.description: Value applied to the attached net.

tools.example: Place .IC 0 V on the oscillator output and 5 V on the supply cap so the transient starts from a realistic state.
tools.notes: Too many .IC constraints can create an unphysical start; prefer .NS where possible.

tools.name: Simulation Generic Components library and global parameters
tools.description: Built-in library (Components panel > Simulation Generic Components) of simulation-ready passives (R, C, L, with tolerance/TC parameters), semiconductors with generic models, sources, transmission lines, switches, digital gates, and directives (.NS, .IC, Parameters/.PARAM, .OPTIONS text). Global parameters are defined with the Parameters directive and referenced in braces {Rload} in component values so sweeps and expressions can use them.
tools.usage: Components panel > Simulation Generic Components; place 'Parameters' directive and add Name/Value pairs; use {Name} in values
tools.example: Parameters directive Rload=1k; R5 value {Rload}; Parameter Sweep on Rload 100 to 10k.
tools.notes: Generic components carry no footprints; replace with real parts (keeping Sim models) before layout or use variants.

tools.name: Signal Integrity setup (Tools > Signal Integrity)
tools.description: Launches the SI analyser from the schematic (pre-layout, using the default stack) or PCB (post-layout using the real layer stack and routing). The setup dialog checks Supply Nets rules and component SI models (IBIS or built-in technology/pin models by component type: IC, Resistor, Capacitor, Connector...), then opens the Signal Integrity panel listing nets with screening results (impedance, falling/rising edge overshoot/undershoot, flight time, slope) against the Signal Integrity rules.
tools.usage: Tools > Signal Integrity... (schematic or PCB); Setup dialog > Model Assignments / Supply Nets > Analyze Design

parameters.name: Supply nets
parameters.description: Nets with voltage from Supply Nets rules.

parameters.name: Model assignments
parameters.description: IBIS or generic technology models per component.

tools.example: Tools > Signal Integrity on the PCB, assign IBIS for U1, Analyze Design, sort by Falling Edge Overshoot, select CLK and run Reflections.
tools.notes: Screening is a fast lumped analysis; Reflection/Crosstalk use the transmission-line model of the layer stack.

tools.name: Signal Integrity: Reflection analysis
tools.description: Simulates the selected nets as transmission lines with driver/receiver IBIS models and the Signal Stimulus rule, plotting waveforms at each pin over time (in a SimData document) so ringing, overshoot and settling can be judged; the Termination Advisor proposes series/parallel/Thevenin/RC/diode terminations and re-simulates with them.
tools.usage: Signal Integrity panel > select net(s) > Reflections button; Termination Advisor > choose termination > Reflections

parameters.name: Termination type
parameters.description: Serial Res, Parallel Res, Thevenin, RC, Diode, Source/Sink options.

tools.example: Select CLK_25M, Reflections: 1.1 V overshoot; Termination Advisor > Serial Res 33 ohm > Reflections shows overshoot 0.3 V.
tools.notes: Results depend on the Signal Stimulus rule and pin electrical models; verify IBIS pin/model mapping.

tools.name: Signal Integrity: Crosstalk analysis
tools.description: Simulates coupling between a victim net and aggressor nets (set via the SI panel's Set Aggressor/Victim commands) using the PCB geometry and layer stack, plotting induced noise on the victim; aggressors receive the Signal Stimulus, victims a constant level. Used with the Parallel Segment rule to bound coupling.
tools.usage: Signal Integrity panel > select victim > Set Victim; select aggressors > Set Aggressor > Crosstalk
tools.example: Victim RESET_N, aggressors CLK_25M and D0: crosstalk plot shows 180 mV coupled noise; increase spacing or add a guard trace.
tools.notes: Only nets sharing a routed parallel section produce meaningful coupling; results appear in the SimData document.

tools.name: IBIS and SI model assignment (Signal Integrity models)
tools.description: Components need a signal-integrity model: an imported IBIS file (Tools > Signal Integrity > Model Assignments > Import IBIS, which maps IBIS pins/models to component pins), or a built-in generic model chosen by Type (IC with technology such as CMOS 3.3V/5V, TTL, LVDS; Resistor, Capacitor, Inductor, Connector, Diode, BJT) with value. Models can be saved back to the schematic component as the SI model link.
tools.usage: Signal Integrity setup > Model Assignments > double-click component > Type/Technology or Import IBIS; 'Update Models in Schematic'

parameters.name: Type / Technology
parameters.description: Generic model family for parts without IBIS.

tools.example: Import STM32F4.ibs for U1, map I/O pins to the IO_3V3 model, click Update Models in Schematic so the assignment persists.
tools.notes: IBIS versions up to the analyser's supported level parse; newer keywords may be ignored with warnings.

tools.name: Simulation Dashboard profiles (save / load analysis setups)
tools.description: The Simulation Dashboard stores the enabled analyses, their parameters, probes, advanced options and output settings with the project; profiles can be saved/loaded to switch between setups (e.g. 'AC_Bode' vs 'Transient_Startup') and the OutJob Simulator output (Netlist outputs > Mixed Sim) runs a saved configuration in batch.
tools.usage: Simulation Dashboard > profile drop-down (Save / Load); Output Job > Simulator outputs
tools.example: Save profile 'Bode' with only AC Sweep enabled; in the OutJob add a Mixed Sim output referencing it and generate the .sdf automatically.
tools.notes: Exact profile file handling differs by version; the dashboard settings are always persisted in the project.
